procedural_matters: SUI 99 was represented by Laurent Chapuis.
HUN 180 did not come to the hearing, the hearing proceeded in accordance with RRS 63.1(b).
Nicola Capriglione (ITA 45) presented evidence during the hearing as a witness for SUI 99.
facts: The conditions at the time of the incident were 12 knots of wind and a 0.5 meter chop.
SUI 99 and HUN 180 were sailing upwind towards mark 1 to be left to port.
SUI 99 was sailing on the starboard layline on starboard tack, and HUN 180 was sailing on the port layline on port tack.
The boats were sailing on a collision course.
SUI 99 entered the zone of the mark on starboard tack.
At the mark HUN 180 luffed and passed head to wind from port to starboard.
Immediately SUI 99 luffed sharply above close-hauled.
There was a contact between SUI 99's front quarter of the port side of the hull and the aft starboard quarter of HUN 180' s hull.
conclusions: After passing head to wind and before being on a close-hauled course, HUN 180 failed to keep clear of SUI
HUN 180 caused SUI 99, who was on starboard tack since entering the zone, to sail above close-hauled to avoid contact. HUN 180 broke RRS 18.3(a).
HUN 180 did not avoid contact with SUI 99 even though it was reasonably possible, and broke RRS 14(a).
It was not reasonably possible for SUI 99, the right-of-way boat to avoid contact with HUN 180 when it became clear that HUN 180 was not keeping clear. SUI 99 did not break RRS 14(a).
